stem: Find the equation of the straight line passing through the point $({=x0}, {=y0})$ and perpendicular to the straight line passing through the two points $A({=xa}, {=ya})$ and $B({=xb}, {=yb})$. Write it in the form $y = mx + b$.
solution: The slope of the line through $A$ and $B$ is $\frac{{=yb} - ({=ya})}{{=xb} - ({=xa})} = \frac{{=yb - ya}}{{=xb - xa}} = {=(yb - ya) / (xb - xa)}$.
The slope of the perpendicular line is the negative reciprocal: $m = {=m}$.
So the equation has the form $y = {=m}x + b$.
The point $({=x0}, {=y0})$ lies on the line: ${=y0} = {=m} \times ({=x0}) + b$.
The equation of the line is $y = {=m}x {=sg} {=abs(b)}$.
notes: AB has slope -1/m so the perpendicular slope is the integer m. Follows book example 3.
